# vet402

> Independent verification of the x402 agent-payment economy. vet402 buys from x402 endpoints, re-reads each payment on-chain, records what came back, checks it against the seller's output declaration when there is one, and publishes the results. It also scores payee wallets on Base, so an x402 API provider or a spending agent can check a counterparty before a payment settles. x402 is an HTTP 402 payment protocol for AI agents. An AI agent pays an x402 API with a stablecoin by answering HTTP 402, often in USDC.

It also matches the sellers it paid to registered ERC-8004 agents. A seller check records past purchases. vet402 does not insure a payment, hold customer funds, or refund a failed one. Cite a figure with its date and the URL it came from. Current figures are at https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/state.

## Key figures (as of 2026-11-25 UTC)

- Paid attempts (`l1.attempts`), on-chain settlements re-read from chain (`l1.settled`), and delivered purchases (`l1.delivered`: settled, then an HTTP 2xx other than 202 Accepted with a non-empty body): read these three fields under `l1` on https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/state (`retrievedAt` is the date to cite). HTML: https://vet402.com/observatory/state. ALLOW, WARN and BLOCK on a seller check are a separate score band from these L1 counts.
- Endpoints attempted (`l1.endpointsAttempted`) and endpoints with at least one delivery (`l1.endpointsDelivered`): same state JSON. HTML: https://vet402.com/observatory/state
- ERC-8004 agents matched to a payTo vet402 paid: `erc8004` in the same state JSON, by chain. HTML: https://vet402.com/observatory/erc8004. Definition: https://vet402.com/erc-8004
- Purchase ledger CSV (`days` from 1 to 366, default window 90 days): https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/export.csv?days=366

## Definitions

- [What is x402?](https://vet402.com/x402): x402 is an open payment standard built on HTTP 402. A server answers 402 with payment terms, the client pays, often in USDC, and repeats the request with proof of payment.
- [What is ERC-8004?](https://vet402.com/erc-8004): ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents) is an Ethereum standard with three registries for AI agents: identity, reputation and validation. Payments are out of its scope.
- [Glossary](https://vet402.com/x402/glossary): facilitator, payTo, PAYMENT-REQUIRED, exact, upto, batch settlement, Bazaar, CAIP-2, agentId, feedbackURI.
- [Methodology](https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology): what L0 (unpaid probe), L1 (real purchase) and L2 (output check against the seller's declaration) mean, and when a failure counts against a seller. One-line definitions: https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology#vocabulary
- [Integrity Terms](https://vet402.com/integrity): the rules vet402 holds itself to, each with its source, the six outcomes one purchase is sorted into and which count against a seller, and what vet402 does not do.

## Check a seller before paying

- [x402 seller reputation API](https://vet402.com/x402/seller-reputation-api): key-less GET /api/v1/check and decision fields (ALLOW, WARN, BLOCK) from real purchases.
- [x402 trust score](https://vet402.com/x402/trust-score): vet402 discontinued the 0 to 100 score in September 2026. Delivery facts and recommendations instead.
- [How a seller check works](https://vet402.com/x402/check-a-seller): read the purchases vet402 made and the ALLOW, WARN or BLOCK decision they support.
- [Check by URL, no key](https://vet402.com/docs/api): `GET https://vet402.com/api/v1/check?url=` followed by the URL-encoded x402 URL
- [Scan a 402 before signing, no key](https://vet402.com/docs/api): `POST https://vet402.com/api/v1/check/presign` with the 402 body the seller returned. Probe latency for one seller checked again and for the first check of distinct sellers (p50, p99, run time): https://vet402.com/data/presign-latency.json
- [Response signatures](https://github.com/vet402/vet402/blob/main/docs/response-signatures.md): Ed25519 over JCS on check, check/presign, find, observatory state, anchors, and delivery sellers JSON. Response header carries the signature. Public keys live at https://vet402.com/.well-known/vet402-keys.json
- [Hosted MCP server](https://vet402.com/docs/mcp): `https://vet402.com/mcp` (streamable HTTP). Tools: check_x402_seller, check_my_x402_endpoint, find_x402_sellers, check_payment_proof, check_8004_agent.
- [Check an ERC-8004 feedback](https://vet402.com/docs/api): `GET https://vet402.com/api/v1/erc8004/check`

## Open data

- [Purchase ledger CSV](https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/export.csv?days=366): paid attempts in the chosen window (up to 366 days), with chain, outcome, and a transaction when one exists.
- [L0 probe CSV](https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/l0/export.csv)
- [Seller delivery feed JSON](https://vet402.com/api/v1/delivery/sellers.json)
- [Bazaar delivery by resource URL](https://vet402.com/api/v1/delivery/by-resource): copy the matching row from the same snapshot as [seller delivery feed JSON](https://vet402.com/api/v1/delivery/sellers.json) onto a CDP Bazaar item `resource` (`GET ?url=` or `POST /api/v1/delivery/annotate` for up to 100 items). Spec: https://github.com/vet402/vet402/blob/main/docs/bazaar-delivery-field.md
- [Fixed snapshots with DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24195171) and [snapshot repository](https://github.com/vet402/vet402-observatory-data)
- [Monthly report: State of x402](https://vet402.com/x402/report/2026-11)
- [Corrections log](https://vet402.com/corrections) and JSON: https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/corrections

## Chains

- [x402 settlements by chain](https://vet402.com/x402/chains): vet402's own L1 purchase counts per chain. It is not ecosystem-wide settlement volume. Base, Solana, Tempo (MPP), XRPL, Arc, Celo, Stellar, Arbitrum One, BNB Chain, Avalanche C-Chain.
- [x402 purchase statistics](https://vet402.com/x402/statistics): paid purchase attempts, settled on-chain, delivered, and counts by chain from `GET /api/v1/observatory/state`.

## Machine-readable pages

Markdown versions of key pages. Lists, terms, definitions and live counts come from the same modules as the HTML. The remaining prose is copied from each page and tests compare it with the page source. methodology.md is a summary: the section headings, the 60-second summary and the one-line definitions. The full text of each section is on the HTML page.

- https://vet402.com/x402/check-a-seller.md: how to check a seller before paying
- https://vet402.com/x402/seller-reputation-api.md: seller reputation API (check and decision)
- https://vet402.com/x402/trust-score.md: what vet402 publishes instead of a 0 to 100 trust score
- https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology.md: L0, L1 and L2 definitions
- https://vet402.com/x402/glossary.md: x402 and ERC-8004 terms
- https://vet402.com/integrity.md: integrity terms and failure attribution
- https://vet402.com/x402/statistics.md: paid purchase counts from the observatory state
- https://vet402.com/erc-8004.md: ERC-8004 and payTo match counts

## Freshness

Every number on this site moves, so it is published with the schedule that moves it rather than as a timeless fact.

- Catalog sync (what is listed, what was delisted): the Bazaar catalog is read in runs scheduled roughly two hours apart, at 00:05 UTC, 02:05 UTC, 04:05 UTC, 06:05 UTC, 08:05 UTC, 10:05 UTC, 12:05 UTC, 14:05 UTC, 16:05 UTC, 18:05 UTC, 20:05 UTC and 22:05 UTC. A run can start later within its scheduled hour. Each run continues from the page where the previous run stopped, so one full read of the Bazaar catalog takes several runs. A Bazaar listing is not marked delisted at present, and that includes a listing that is also in the Circle x402 discovery. The MPP directory is fetched once a day, at 01:30 UTC. A listing that leaves the MPP directory is not judged delisted until the next complete 01:30 UTC fetch. The Circle x402 discovery is fetched at 01:30 UTC. A listing that leaves the Circle x402 discovery is not judged delisted until the next complete fetch of that catalog. vet402 also measures a short checked-in list of sellers it adds itself, https://github.com/vet402/vet402/blob/main/src/lib/observatory/operator-listings.ts, synced at 01:30 UTC and shown as listed_in `operator`; each entry names its reason and date, a POST entry holds the example body vet402 sends when the seller's 402 declares none (recorded as request_body `operator_example`), and sellers cannot pay or ask to be added.
- L0 probes: scheduled at 10:30 UTC, and the operator adds runs. Further runs at 00:30 UTC, 02:30 UTC, 06:30 UTC, 14:30 UTC, 18:30 UTC and 22:30 UTC probe listings with no L0 probe in the last 7 days first. The daily metrics rollup: 10:30 UTC.
- L1 purchases: several runs a day. The scheduled run is 12:00 UTC; the operator adds runs at 00:00, 06:00 and 18:00 UTC, and further runs at 03:30, 09:30, 15:30 and 21:30 UTC. Read the time of each attempt from the ledger (`/api/v1/observatory/export.csv`) rather than from this list. On-chain settlement re-read: daily, 14:00 UTC. Most `settle_claimed` rows move to `settled` (or `settle_claim_refuted`) at the first re-read after the attempt, but a row stays at `settle_claimed` while the chain read cannot settle it either way, so some rows wait far longer than a day. Read the current count, the counts older than 1 and 7 days and the oldest attempt from `l1.awaitingReread`, `l1.awaitingRereadOlderThan1d`, `l1.awaitingRereadOlderThan7d` and `l1.awaitingRereadOldestAttemptAt` on `/api/v1/observatory/state` rather than assuming a day.
- Caches: the longest a copy you receive can lag the database, per surface. A shared-cache copy is served fresh for `s-maxage` and, with `stale-while-revalidate`, for that much longer while a fresh one is computed, so the most it can lag is the sum of the two. The `Age` response header says how long the copy you received sat in the cache. The `Cache-Control` values below are what each route sets: the CDN removes `s-maxage` and `stale-while-revalidate` from the copy you receive and keeps `max-age`, so the header you see can read just `public`. A page and the JSON can therefore show different numbers for a while after a run — compare their retrieval times rather than assume either is newer.
  - HTML pages that print observatory or /sellers aggregates (/, /observatory, /observatory/state, /sellers): rendered on every request, reading the aggregates through a 5-minute data cache (`PUBLIC_READ_REVALIDATE`, 300 s). A read after the window is served the older copy once while the fresh one is computed, so after a quiet spell one page view can be older than 5 minutes.
  - `GET /api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/decision`: no `Cache-Control`; each server instance reuses a decision it computed for up to 5 minutes (`DECISION_CACHE_TTL_MS`), so a copy can be up to 5 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/state`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800`. A copy can be up to 45 minutes old. On a miss the aggregates come from the same 5-minute data cache as the HTML pages, so a copy can be older by that much, or more once after a quiet spell. `retrievedAt` in the body is when the aggregates were read.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/decisions`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800`. A copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/l0/export.csv`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800`. A copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/sellers/export.csv`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800`. A copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/accuracy`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=1200`. A copy can be up to 30 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/endpoints/{id}/purchases`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=1200`. A copy can be up to 30 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/delivery.csv`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=7200`. A copy can be up to 3 hours old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/export.csv`, `/history`, `/anchors`, `/traceable-by-chain`, `/backtest`, `/concentration`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=7200`. A copy can be up to 3 hours old.
  - `GET /api/v1/census/summary`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=900`. A copy can be up to 20 minutes old.
  - key-less object reads (`/api/v1/resolve`, `/resources/{id}`, `/endpoints/{id}`, `/endpoints/{id}/payees`, `/payees/{address}/endpoints`, `/observatory/endpoints/{id}/facts`, `/observatory/corrections`): `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`. A copy can be up to 6 minutes old.
  - `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`. A copy can be up to 1 hour old.
- `retrievedAt` in the JSON (`generatedAt` on `/api/v1/accuracy`, the `x-vet402-retrieved-at` header on the CSV) is the time vet402 read the numbers from its database, not the time you asked. It travels inside the cached copy, so it stays true whichever copy you were served, and it is the date to cite.

A measurement quoted without its retrieval date is not a measurement. Take the date from `retrievedAt` in the JSON, from the `x-vet402-retrieved-at` header on the CSV, or from the day you fetched the page.
